primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Familial isolated hypoparathyroidism due to GCM2 loss of function
mechanism: GCM2 is a transcription factor and master regulator of parathyroid development. Loss-of-function variants can impair parathyroid development or function, producing inappropriately low PTH, hypocalcemia, and hyperphosphatemia without the broader phenotype of syndromic hypoparathyroidism.
vignette: A 6-year-old boy is evaluated for recurrent carpopedal spasm. Serum calcium is low, phosphate is high, magnesium is normal, and parathyroid hormone is markedly low. Renal function is normal. He has no cardiac defect, facial dysmorphism, hearing loss, or mucocutaneous candidiasis. His older sister has the same biochemical findings. Genetic testing identifies a biallelic loss-of-function variant in GCM2.
lead: Which normal developmental process is most directly disrupted by this mutation?
correct: Transcriptional regulation required for development of the parathyroid glands
distractors: Migration of neural crest cells into the cardiac outflow tract
Activation of the calcium-sensing receptor in mature parathyroid chief cells
Renal conversion of 25-hydroxyvitamin D to 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D
End-organ signaling through the PTH/PTHrP receptor in bone and kidney
distractor_notes: Neural crest migration defects can contribute to syndromic findings such as conotruncal abnormalities but do not explain isolated familial GCM2-associated hypoparathyroidism.
Activating CaSR variants suppress PTH secretion but do not represent the developmental role of GCM2 specified by the genotype.
1-alpha-hydroxylase deficiency causes impaired calcitriol synthesis with secondary hyperparathyroidism rather than markedly low PTH.
PTH resistance causes elevated PTH because target organs fail to respond; it does not explain low PTH from a GCM2 defect.
key_expl: GCM2 is a master transcriptional regulator of parathyroid development. Loss-of-function variants can cause familial isolated hypoparathyroidism, leading to low PTH, hypocalcemia, and hyperphosphatemia.
objective: Connect GCM2 loss of function with defective parathyroid development and familial isolated hypoparathyroidism.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Familial nonautoimmune hyperthyroidism due to activating TSHR variants
mechanism: Germline gain-of-function variants in TSHR can constitutively activate TSH-receptor signaling in thyroid follicular cells, increasing thyroid hormone synthesis and growth despite suppressed pituitary TSH and absent stimulating autoantibodies.
vignette: A 12-year-old girl has weight loss, tremor, tachycardia, and a diffuse goiter. Free thyroxine is elevated and TSH is suppressed. TSH-receptor antibodies and thyroid peroxidase antibodies are absent. Her father and paternal grandmother developed similar antibody-negative hyperthyroidism during childhood. Genetic testing identifies a heterozygous TSHR variant.
lead: Which functional effect of this variant most likely causes the disorder?
correct: Constitutive activation of TSH-receptor signaling in thyroid follicular cells in the absence of ligand
distractors: Reduced TSH-receptor signaling that increases pituitary TSH secretion
Production of an immunoglobulin that binds and stimulates the TSH receptor
Failure of thyroid peroxidase to organify iodide
Increased peripheral conversion of thyroxine to triiodothyronine without increased thyroid hormone synthesis
distractor_notes: Inactivating TSHR variants produce TSH resistance and hypothyroidism, not familial hyperthyroidism with suppressed TSH.
Stimulating immunoglobulins cause Graves disease, but the family has antibody-negative nonautoimmune hyperthyroidism.
Thyroid peroxidase deficiency impairs hormone synthesis and causes hypothyroidism/goiter.
Isolated increased peripheral conversion does not account for hereditary goiter and autonomous thyroid stimulation by a TSHR variant.
key_expl: Familial nonautoimmune hyperthyroidism is caused by germline activating TSHR variants. Constitutive receptor activity drives thyroid hormone synthesis and thyroid growth even when pituitary TSH is suppressed.
objective: Recognize constitutive TSH-receptor activation as the mechanism of autosomal-dominant antibody-negative familial hyperthyroidism.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Familial hyperaldosteronism type III due to KCNJ5 dysfunction
mechanism: Gain-of-function KCNJ5 variants reduce potassium-channel selectivity so sodium enters zona glomerulosa cells. Membrane depolarization opens voltage-gated calcium channels; increased intracellular calcium activates signaling that increases aldosterone synthesis and can promote adrenal hyperplasia.
vignette: A 15-year-old boy has severe hypertension, hypokalemia, metabolic alkalosis, suppressed plasma renin activity, and markedly elevated aldosterone. Both adrenal glands are enlarged. His mother had severe childhood hypertension. Genetic testing identifies a germline KCNJ5 variant associated with familial hyperaldosteronism type III.
lead: Which sequence of cellular events most directly increases aldosterone production in this disorder?
correct: Loss of potassium-channel selectivity → sodium influx and membrane depolarization → calcium influx → increased aldosterone synthesis
distractors: Increased potassium efflux → membrane hyperpolarization → reduced calcium influx → increased aldosterone synthesis
Reduced epithelial sodium-channel activity in the collecting duct → hyperkalemia → suppressed aldosterone synthesis
Constitutive activation of the ACTH receptor → increased cortisol synthesis → secondary suppression of aldosterone
Inhibition of angiotensin II receptors on zona glomerulosa cells → reduced calcium signaling → increased aldosterone synthesis
distractor_notes: The mutant channel is less selective and permits sodium influx, producing depolarization rather than hyperpolarization.
ENaC loss causes salt wasting and hyperkalemia and stimulates rather than suppresses aldosterone.
Familial hyperaldosteronism type III is driven by KCNJ5 ion-channel abnormalities, not constitutive ACTH receptor activation.
Angiotensin II receptor inhibition lowers aldosterone; it cannot explain autonomous excess.
key_expl: KCNJ5 mutations in familial hyperaldosteronism type III make the potassium channel less selective. Sodium entry depolarizes adrenal glomerulosa cells, opening calcium channels and increasing calcium-dependent aldosterone synthesis.
objective: Trace the ion-channel mechanism linking KCNJ5 loss of potassium selectivity to calcium-dependent aldosterone excess.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Aldosterone synthase deficiency due to CYP11B2 dysfunction
mechanism: CYP11B2, expressed in the zona glomerulosa, catalyzes the terminal mitochondrial reactions converting deoxycorticosterone derivatives to aldosterone. Inactivating variants cause isolated hypoaldosteronism with salt wasting and high renin while cortisol and sex-steroid synthesis remain intact.
vignette: A 3-week-old infant is admitted for poor feeding, vomiting, weight loss, dehydration, hyponatremia, and hyperkalemia. Plasma renin activity is markedly elevated and aldosterone is very low. Cortisol and 17-hydroxyprogesterone are normal, and there is no genital ambiguity. An older sibling had a similar salt-wasting illness in infancy that improved with age.
lead: Deficiency of which enzyme most directly explains these findings?
distractors: 21-hydroxylase (CYP21A2)
11-beta-hydroxylase (CYP11B1)
17-alpha-hydroxylase (CYP17A1)
Cholesterol side-chain cleavage enzyme (CYP11A1)
distractor_notes: 21-hydroxylase deficiency impairs cortisol and often aldosterone and is associated with elevated 17-hydroxyprogesterone and androgen excess.
11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency causes excess deoxycorticosterone and low-renin hypertension rather than salt wasting.
17-alpha-hydroxylase deficiency causes low-renin hypertension and deficient sex steroids.
CYP11A1 deficiency reduces essentially all adrenal and gonadal steroids rather than producing isolated hypoaldosteronism with normal cortisol.
key_expl: Aldosterone synthase deficiency is an inherited CYP11B2 defect. It produces hyperreninemic hypoaldosteronism and infantile salt wasting while cortisol and sex-steroid synthesis are preserved.
objective: Differentiate isolated CYP11B2 aldosterone synthase deficiency from other steroidogenic enzyme defects using renin, aldosterone, cortisol, 17-hydroxyprogesterone, and blood-pressure patterns.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
diagnosis: Lipoid congenital adrenal hyperplasia due to STAR dysfunction
mechanism: STAR normally mediates the rate-limiting transfer of cholesterol into mitochondria for steroidogenesis. Severe STAR deficiency causes profound reduction of adrenal and gonadal steroids; compensatory trophic stimulation drives cholesterol accumulation and progressive steroidogenic-cell injury.
vignette: A 2-month-old infant with a 46,XY karyotype is evaluated for recurrent vomiting, dehydration, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, and hypotension. The external genitalia are female. Cortisol, aldosterone, and adrenal androgens are all very low; ACTH and plasma renin activity are markedly elevated. Ultrasonography shows bilaterally enlarged adrenal glands containing abundant lipid. There is no elevation of 17-hydroxyprogesterone.
lead: Which diagnosis best explains this presentation?
correct: Lipoid congenital adrenal hyperplasia due to steroidogenic acute regulatory protein deficiency
distractors: 21-hydroxylase deficiency
11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency
17-alpha-hydroxylase deficiency
Androgen insensitivity syndrome
distractor_notes: 21-hydroxylase deficiency typically elevates 17-hydroxyprogesterone and adrenal androgens; 46,XY infants are not typically phenotypic females from absent androgen synthesis.
11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency causes androgen excess and deoxycorticosterone-mediated hypertension.
17-alpha-hydroxylase deficiency can cause undervirilization but produces mineralocorticoid-mediated hypertension and hypokalemia rather than salt-wasting shock.
Androgen insensitivity causes female external genitalia in 46,XY individuals but adrenal steroid production, sodium, potassium, cortisol, and aldosterone are not globally deficient.
key_expl: STAR deficiency prevents efficient transfer of cholesterol into mitochondria, sharply reducing all adrenal and gonadal steroid synthesis. A 46,XY infant can therefore have female external genitalia and severe salt-wasting adrenal insufficiency; lipid accumulates in stimulated steroidogenic cells.
objective: Recognize STAR-related lipoid congenital adrenal hyperplasia from global steroid deficiency, salt wasting, 46,XY undervirilization, and lipid-laden enlarged adrenals.
duplicate_probe_terms: all steroid products low lipid adrenal
